To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
projectile fragmentation of 238 U on 208 Pb target at 750 A Mev bombarding energy was investigated with the FRS.
the production cross sections of medium-weight isotopic fragments from the projectile 238U were measured at a bombarding energies of 750 AMeV in collisions with a lead target.

the projectile-fragmentation of 238U on a Pb target at a bombarding-energy of 750 AMeV was investigated and the isotopic production cross sections for about 250 different fragments in the Z range from 30 to 53 were measured.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the reaction mechanisms involved in heavy-ion induced fragmentation reactions.
the investigation of projectile fragmentation reactions at intermediate energies.
the production and identification of projectile fragments from a heavy projectile.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fragmentation process is not a simple one.
the fragmentation process is very complex and that the production of the medium-weight isotopes is governed by several competing mechanisms.

the measured production cross sections of projectile fragments and fission products in the reaction of 238U on a 208Pb target at 750 A Me V bombarding energy are in good agreement with the predictions of the code CASCADE, which is used for the analysis of the measured data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have measured the production cross sections of more than 100 isotopes in the mass range A= 80-150 in a single experiment and that we have been able to identify the fragmentation residues.
the production of medium-weight isotopic chains is dominated by fission, while the production of heavy and light fragments is dominated by projectile fragmentation.
the measured isotopic production cross sections can be described by an evaporation code, if a large number of evaporation steps is allowed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production of neutron-rich isotopes in the mass region around A= 130 can be significantly enhanced by projectile fragmentation.
the measured production cross sections are consistent with the expectations from a statistical model, which indicates that the measured isotopes are in equilibrium with their environment.
the fragmentation of 238 U in 208 Pb collisions is a violent process, which leads to the production of many medium-weight isotopes.
